text:
Five more, quickly. A model registry versions trained artifacts with their metadata: the data version, hyperparameters, evaluation metrics and deployment history. It enforces promotion from staging to production, and turns a rollback into a lookup rather than a rebuild. Retraining has four triggers: a schedule, a drift alert, live accuracy or a proxy falling below a threshold, and enough new labeled data. Continuous training automates them, and every version it produces goes through the same gate and staged rollout. Blue-green keeps two full environments. Blue serves while green gets the new model and warms up; traffic flips in one switch, and flips back if anything breaks. Near-zero downtime and instant rollback, for the cost of running both. A canary is the gradual version. Experiment tracking, with tools like em-el-flow or Weights and Biases, logs every run's hyperparameters, metrics, code version and artifacts. Without it, nobody can say which run made the model in production. And to package a model, serialize the artifact, pin the runtime and dependencies, and build a container so serving matches training. Exporting to onyx, a framework-neutral format, frees it from the training library and opens faster runtimes.

Versioned, gated, watched and reversible: that's a model you can leave running. Large language models bring a serving problem of their own: generation is slow and memory-hungry. Next: serving LLMs.
